messages.subject: Count repeated measure in ez!
parts:
Hi, I had googled and found this great job. However, I am not sure if
I could do my task with ez. Here is one example of my data:

Specie Mother Treatment Rep 1dias 2dias 3dias 4dias 5dias 6dias 7dias
Sucupira M02 Germinação 1 0 1 1 1 1 1 1
Sucupira M02 Germinação 2 0 0 0 0 0 2 3
Sucupira M02 Germinação 3 0 0 0 0 0 0 1
Sucupira M04 Germinação 1 0 0 0 0 1 1 1
(...)
Vinhatico M15CV15 Infestação 3 0 0 4 4 5 7 8

Each rep I had a gerbox (plot) with 20 seeds from each mother. The
following treatments was counted in same plot.

Treatment "Germinação" I count how much seeds had germinated each day.
Treatment "Infestação" I count how much seeds had pathogens each day.

This two treatment was counted in the same plot (20 seeds).

Is it possible to do this task with ez?

Thank you very much!

Marcelo

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Count repeated measure in ez!
parts:
You'll have to re-organize your data into what is called "long" data
format. This can be achieved by:

install.packages('reshape2') #not necessary if it's already installed
library(reshape2)
my_long_data = melt.data.frame(
data = my_data
, id.vars = c('Specie','Mother','Treatment','Rep')
, variable_name = 'Dias'
)

Then you can perform your ANOVA. However, I suspect that ANOVA is not
the right tool for you. Count data is unlikely to be Gaussian
distributed, so you'll want a statistical tool that can provide a link
to a more appropriate error distribution, like the poisson
distribution. Also, I suspect that your design would benefit from
being able to specify multiple random effects (from what you describe,
it sounds like gerbox and mother are crossed random effects). So, I'd
look into mixed effects modelling if I were you. Here are a couple
good resource pages:

http://lme4.r-forge.r-project.org

http://glmm.wikidot.com

http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/tagged/mixed-model
